document.abstract: On October 21, 1999 the U.S. Association of Imaging Technology and Sound held a Legislative Action Day at which 13 of its members petitioned 22 members of Congress for technology related tax relief. Unfortunately, no archivists were reported to have participated in these meetings! It is important for archivists around the world to develop digital asset management policies that can serve to direct standards efforts that bring some order to this chaos. Today, SMPTE/ANSI Standards cover a very limited scope, pertaining largely to signal structures and product interchange between devices and media manufacturers. At the same time, in the absence of much needed standards covering content exchange, the post-production and archival communities are left to seek taxpayer relief to cope with the rapid changes in technology. This situation deserves serious industry consideration.

authors.bio: Ed H. Zwaneveld has directed technological research and development at the National Film Board of Canada since 1982. He has been responsible for more than 150 research and development projects that have advanced the state of technology with increased efficiency and creative latitude in film and television production, post-production, distribution, and the management of A/V assets. As a member of the Canadian Task Force on the Preservation and Enhanced Use of Canada's A/V Heritage, Zwaneveld initiated work to modernize media asset preservation processes and develop appropriate practices for the extended-term preservation, migration, and use of audiovisual works on magnetic media. Currently, he chairs the SMPTE V 16.07 Work Group on Archival Storage Magnetic Media and the AMIA Preservation Committee. He is a is Team Leader of Work Package 1 on Legacy Archives of the EBU/IFTA Project Group on Future Television Archives (P/FTA). He is also technical advisor to the CBC/SRC and WGBH-Boston on television archiving solutions. A SMPTE Fellow, Zwaneveld is the recipient of its Technicolor/ Herbert T. Kalmus Gold Medal Award and Samuel L. Warner Memorial Medal Award; an AMPAS Technical Achievement Academy Award; and an Outstanding Achievement Award in Engineering Development from NATAS. He has authored and published 70 technical and research papers in four languages. Educated in the Netherlands, he holds a degree in mechanical engineering and is a member of the FKTG (Berlin), BKSTS (London), and the IBC Council (London).
